Day/night mode and image format/quality apply immediately. Other display and streaming changes reconnect the iPhone.
Audio output changes apply immediately. Changing the microphone source reconnects the iPhone.
Changes apply the next time the iPhone connects.
If your head unit can install Android apps, try DiPlay for a better experience. WheelPlay provides CarPlay through a browser without modifying the head unit.
No valid resources configured · Import to enable CarPlay
Use the last connection method and selected iPhone.
Requires the system to allow automatic startup.
This device creates a Wi-Fi Direct network for the iPhone.
Enable the hotspot in system settings, then enter the same name and password here. The iPhone will join this network. Changes apply on the next connection.
Switches immediately. Falls back to Android when the browser is not ready or is offline. You may need to tap the browser page to enable sound.
Reconnects after changes. The browser microphone requires trusted HTTPS and permission; Android is used until it is ready. Disabling stops uploads and removes the microphone capability.
Sent to the iPhone immediately. Follow Android uses this service device\'s system day/night mode.
Adjust the size of CarPlay icons and text. Applying reconnects the iPhone.

Add margins where head-unit controls cover the edges, scaled to the display resolution. Saving reconnects the iPhone to lay out CarPlay inside the safe area. Touch coordinates still cover the full display.
Negotiate the CarPlay resolution using the browser\'s actual aspect ratio. Browser size changes reconnect the iPhone.
WebRTC passes H.264 / HEVC through and falls back to image streaming (about 15 fps) if unsupported. Set the negotiated frame rate to 60 for 60 fps. Check the web page for the actual frame rate.

Keep the last frame and wait for recovery during brief interruptions. Fall back to JPEG only after the selected interval. This adds no video buffering; unsupported codecs and failed connections still fall back immediately. Applies on the next browser connection.
Applies on the next connection. Requires browser HEVC / WebRTC support, otherwise falls back to JPEG. Uses H.264 when disabled.
Move CarPlay controls to the right.
The highlighted region is the CarPlay layout area. Each margin accepts 0–40%; 0 means no margin.
Each margin must be a whole number from 0–40%
Shown as the return-to-vehicle entry in CarPlay. The name and icon can be changed independently. Applies on the next iPhone connection.
Drag, zoom and crop an image to a square. The icon is stored on this device and remains available after the original image is deleted.
The name and icon will revert to NIO. Applies on the next iPhone connection.

The iPhone and navigation app provide location by default. Selecting Android sends this device\'s location when requested by the iPhone and requires precise location permission. Applies on the next iPhone connection.
Show navigation arrows, distance and road names. Support depends on the vehicle.
Defaults to wheelplay.local. Use the HTTP listener port on the same local network. The head unit\'s network must allow multicast.
Enter a single-label .local hostname, such as wheelplay.local

Listener settings do not require root. The hostname is used for HTTP and HTTPS and must resolve to the access IP. Entering it does not configure DNS. Custom HTTPS certificates must cover this hostname.
Provide HTTPS access for browsers. Browser microphones require a trusted certificate.
Certificates and keys are stored privately in the app. For PEM, select the certificate chain, then the private key. PKCS#12 supports selecting a private-key entry.
Helps head units that block private IP ranges access this phone\'s local service. Head units from other manufacturers with similar restrictions may also work.
Requires Android VPN permission, without root or Shizuku. May conflict with other VPNs.

Connect the head unit to this phone\'s system hotspot and open http://%1$s:%2$d. Some phones or head units may be incompatible, and system updates may affect support. If wired CarPlay is connected, enabling or changing the IP waits until it disconnects.
Uses the Web listener ports directly, without low-port forwarding. Optional HTTPS still requires a trusted certificate on the head unit. WebRTC video needs separate testing.
Share HTTP / HTTPS low ports and a custom IP with hotspot clients.

Forwarding applies only to this access IP and does not change the Web listener ports. HTTPS forwarding applies only when HTTPS is enabled. Enable the system hotspot; custom certificates must cover the access IP or hostname.
Resources ready · Private key and certificate verified
The open-source APK does not include authentication resources. Select your two existing files, or download and import the official DiPlay APK. Installing DiPlay is not required.
Download the APK, then return to import it or share it with WheelPlay
Only authentication resources are extracted and stored privately on this device; nothing is uploaded. The temporary APK is deleted after import. Uninstalling WheelPlay deletes imported resources.
First select identity.pk8 (PKCS#8 private key), then certificate.p7b (P-256 certificate). Both must belong to the same identity. Canceling or failed validation preserves existing resources.

Nearby devices permission connects the iPhone; the microphone is used for Siri and calls. Wireless connections on older Android versions also require location permission. USB mode may request local VPN permission.
Saved to Downloads/WheelPlay. Reports are not uploaded automatically and exclude protocol payloads and credentials.
Choose where to save the report. Reports are not uploaded automatically and exclude protocol payloads and credentials.
Based on xcertplay / DiPlay, retaining GPL-3.0 and AGPL-3.0 license notices. CarPlay and NIO icons belong to their respective owners.
HTTPS is disabled. Enable it in Web service settings.
HTTPS is starting or failed to start. Try again shortly.
Before installing the certificate on the head unit, compare every character of the SHA-256 fingerprint with the browser page:\n\n%1$s
Paired browsers are remembered and reconnect automatically. After choosing startup options, tap Start display on the web page.
The timer starts when a CarPlay session has no connected browser. Reconnecting cancels the timer. A timeout disconnects only the iPhone; the Web service keeps running.
No remembered browsers yet. Scan the QR code or enter the pairing code on the web page to pair one.
Current browser connections will disconnect. All browsers will need to scan or enter a pairing code next time.
Listener port must be between 1024 and 65535
Listener port saved. Reconnect browsers using the new address
Forwarded port must be between 1 and 1023

JPEG prioritizes compatibility. WebP can save bandwidth but may require more encoding CPU. Unsupported browsers use JPEG. Applies to image compatibility mode and WebRTC fallback, without reconnecting.

Default: 75. Higher values preserve more detail and usually use more bandwidth. JPEG and WebP quality values are not equivalent. Saving also refreshes a static image; WebRTC video quality is unaffected.
Enter a whole number from 1 to 100.
